battle.title: Stack Smash Arena
battle.description: Push, pop and peek your way through LIFO puzzles and bracket traps.

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes a stack?
options: First in, first out: the oldest item is removed first
Items are always removed in sorted order
Last in, first out: the most recently pushed item is removed first
Any item can be removed in constant time by its position
questions.answer: Last in, first out: the most recently pushed item is removed first
questions.explanation: A stack only exposes its top, so push and pop work on the newest item. FIFO describes a queue, which is the tempting mix-up.
After three pushes the top is 3, pop removes it, so peek shows 2 and two items remain. Many learners forget that pop already removed 3 before peek.

questions.text: A text editor must undo the most recent edit first, then the one before it. Which structure fits best?
options: A sorted array of edit actions
A hash set of edit actions
questions.explanation: Undo always reverses the newest action, which is exactly LIFO. A queue would undo the oldest edit first, which is wrong for undo.

questions.text: What does this program print? (ArrayDeque prints from the top of the stack.)
questions.explanation: push adds at the front, so the stack is [3, 2, 1]; pop removes 3 and push(4) gives [4, 2, 1]. Reading [1, 2, 4] forgets that the top is printed first.

questions.text: A bracket checker uses a stack on the string "([)]". When does it report the string as unbalanced?
options: At the third character: ')' arrives but the top is '['
At the end, because the stack still holds '('
At the second character, because '[' follows '('
It never does, because the counts of each bracket are equal
questions.answer: At the third character: ')' arrives but the top is '['
questions.explanation: After pushing '(' and '[', the ')' must match the top '[', which it does not, so it fails immediately. Counting brackets alone would wrongly accept this string.

coding.title: Balanced Brackets
coding.description: Given a string made only of the characters ( ) [ ] { }, decide whether the brackets are balanced. Every opener must be closed by the same type of bracket in the correct nesting order. The empty string is balanced. Print YES or NO.
coding.inputDescription: One line containing the bracket string (it may be empty).

debug.title: Postfix Backwards
debug.description: The program reads one line holding a postfix expression with integers and the operators + - * separated by spaces, and prints its value. It gives wrong answers whenever the operator is minus. Input: one line. Output: one integer.
hints: Try the input '5 2 -'. What should it print and what does the program print?
Look at how the two operands are taken off the stack before the operator is applied.
The first pop returns the right-hand operand, not the left one. The operands are swapped.
Pop b first, then a, and compute a op b so the order of subtraction is correct.
